subject.title: [Feature] Queue prompts when API limits prevent an immediate response

question: Should this provider-limit prompt queue remain a narrow standalone tracker, or should it be folded into the broader run-lifecycle reliability design at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/101863?
rationale: The fix crosses provider fallback, session state, user-visible delivery, durable storage, and sensitive prompt persistence, so automation should not choose the permanent product boundary or storage contract.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow core queue
options.body: Keep this issue as the canonical provider-capacity tracker and require a SQLite-backed implementation coordinated with the broader lifecycle design.

options.title: Fold into lifecycle design
options.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/101863 the canonical owner and close this only after its Track C/D scope explicitly includes provider-limit capacity waits.

options.title: Reject automatic capacity queueing
options.body: Keep provider-limit failures as visible terminal/cooldown states and leave automatic retry/queue behavior to a future explicit policy.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrow core queue
recommendation.body: Keep this issue as the canonical provider-capacity tracker and require a SQLite-backed implementation coordinated with the broader lifecycle design.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent combined history across queue lifecycle, provider fallback, auth state, and database-first storage decisions.
